messages.subject: Segmentation fault on Ubuntu 16.04.06
parts:
INLA runs nicely on my local Ubuntu 18 notebook for small problems, but does crash on an Ubuntu 16.06.4 server with more memory that I need for larger problems.

I installed INLA by following:
http://www.r-inla.org/download
Installing a special compiled version on the server will require hassle and a lot of communication.

The verbose option does not help with output.
What can I do to locate the problem and hopefully fix it?

Here is a little example taken from this forum:

library(INLA)
INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround()

n = 300
x1 = rnorm(n, sd=0.2)
x2 = rnorm(n, sd=0.2)
eps = rnorm(n,  sd = 0.1)
eta = x1 + x2 + eps
y = exp(eta) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)

r = inla(y ~ -1 + x1 + x2 + f(idx),
         data = data.frame(y, x1, x2, idx = 1:n),
         verbose = TRUE,
         control.family = list(
           control.link = list(
             model = "log")))
The output is:
Segmentation fault
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Segmentation fault on Ubuntu 16.04.06
parts:
On Mon, 2019-10-21 at 08:28 -0700, tw...@bgc-jena.mpg.de wrote:
> INLA runs nicely on my local Ubuntu 18 notebook for small problems,
> but does crash on an Ubuntu 16.06.4 server with more memory that I
> need for larger problems.

install the most recent testing version

inla.upgrade(testing=T)

restart R

do

inla.binary.install()

you may chose the CentOS7 one or the Ubuntu16.04 one. The CentOS7 is
what I run on our Ubuntu 16 server.

then you should be fine.

--
Håvard Rue
Helpdesk
he...@r-inla.org

sorry,

messages.author: 216dc199b6cf5729
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Segmentation fault on Ubuntu 16.04.06
parts:
This solved the issue with simple user-rights.

For users with similar problems: Restarting the R session in RStudio-Server was not enough, and I got errors during binary install. However, terminating R from the session menu worked for me.

Many thanks
Thomas
